name: Advanced Diploma of Accounting
description:
This qualification (FNS60222) sits above the standard Diploma of Accounting as the next rung for people already working in accounting or bookkeeping roles who want to move into more senior positions without doing a full university degree. There's no work placement requirement built in, which reflects that most students taking this at South Metro TAFE are already employed in the industry and studying around their job rather than starting from zero.

Delivery leans heavily online with mandatory on-campus attendance for assessments, and the college is upfront that students should budget 10-15 hours a week of study outside class time: assignment prep, private study and research on top of scheduled contact hours. That's a meaningful time commitment for people who are often studying part-time while working full-time, which is the more common profile for this level of qualification than a straight-from-school student.

The practical payoff is Tax Practitioners Board recognition: complete the prescribed taxation units and pass them, and graduates become eligible to pursue registration as a Registered Tax Agent, a credential that opens up self-employed tax practice or more senior roles in accounting firms handling client tax affairs.
curriculum:
Core units: complex corporate reporting requirements, financial reports for corporate entities, management accounting systems, budgets and forecasts, tax documentation for legal entities
Elective units: audit and assurance practice, financial risk management, specialised tax practices (prescribed units required for Tax Practitioners Board pathway)
Delivery: predominantly online with mandatory on-campus attendance for scheduled assessments
No mandatory work placement; approximately 10-15 hours per week of self-directed study expected outside class
Pathway: eligible graduates (with prescribed taxation units) can pursue Registered Tax Agent recognition through the Tax Practitioners Board

Advanced Diploma of Civil and Structural Engineering

Diploma of Accounting
description:
The standard-level Diploma of Accounting (FNS50222) is the more common entry point into professional accounting study at South Metro TAFE, sitting below the Advanced Diploma and typically taken by people who haven't yet worked in the field rather than those already employed and upskilling. It shares the same no-mandatory-placement structure as the Advanced Diploma: the assumption is that competency is demonstrated through simulated business scenarios and assessment tasks rather than a supervised workplace stint.

Like its advanced counterpart, delivery is mostly online with scheduled on-campus attendance for assessments, and the college flags 10-15 hours a week of expected self-directed study on top of scheduled contact. Accounting coursework tends to be assignment-heavy and cumulative, so falling behind on one unit's calculations makes the next unit noticeably harder.

Graduates commonly move into bookkeeping, accounts assistant or accounts payable/receivable roles, and the diploma functions as a credit-bearing pathway into further study, either the Advanced Diploma for those wanting Tax Agent registration eligibility, or articulation into a related university accounting degree for students who decide partway through that they want the fuller qualification.
curriculum:
Core units: financial reports preparation for reporting entities, management accounting systems, tax documentation for individual and business clients, budgeting and forecasting
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include payroll systems, business software applications, workplace financial systems)
Delivery: predominantly online with mandatory on-campus attendance for scheduled assessments
No mandatory work placement; approximately 10-15 hours per week of self-directed study expected outside class
Pathway: articulation into Advanced Diploma of Accounting or related university accounting/commerce degrees

name: Diploma of Apparel, Fashion and Textiles
Diploma of Business
description:
The Diploma of Business at South Metro TAFE is the deliberately broad option in the college's business suite. Where the Diploma of Accounting and Diploma of Hospitality Management lock students into a named discipline from the start, this qualification builds general business administration, project coordination and leadership competencies that apply across office environments regardless of sector.

That breadth is the point rather than a shortcoming: students who aren't sure yet whether they want to specialise into accounting, marketing, HR or operations get a year to build transferable skills and figure out direction, and the qualification is commonly used as a stepping stone into supervisory or team-leader roles in whatever industry a student happens to already be working in, rather than requiring a career change to make use of it.

As with the other business-suite diplomas at the college, there's no mandatory industry placement; assessment relies on workplace simulations and, where students are already employed, real workplace projects and evidence drawn from their existing job.
curriculum:
Core units: business innovation and improvement processes, workplace health and safety systems, business risk management, project scope and objectives, team leadership and workplace communication
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include human resources fundamentals, marketing principles, business technology and systems)
No mandatory work placement; assessment via workplace simulation and, for employed students, real workplace project evidence
Study load: approximately 10-15 hours per week of self-directed study expected outside scheduled class time

name: Diploma of Civil and Structural Engineering
Diploma of Community Services
description:
Entry into South Metropolitan TAFE's Diploma of Community Services (CHC52021) generally expects a Certificate IV in Community Services already completed, or equivalent industry experience: it's pitched at people who've already had some exposure to the sector rather than a first qualification for someone entirely new to community work. The approximately 240 hours of mandatory work placement is arranged by the college itself rather than left to students to source, and comes with its own logbook system that both the student and the host workplace need to complete.

Because placements put students into direct contact with vulnerable community members, the compliance requirements are more involved than for most other diplomas at this level: a Working With Children Check and National Police Clearance are required before placement starts, and students must be 18 or over to go on placement at all, an industry-wide requirement rather than something specific to this college.

Graduates typically move into case work, community support, disability services or youth work roles, and the diploma level is often the practical ceiling for direct-service roles before further specialisation (such as a related degree) becomes necessary for case management or supervisory positions.
curriculum:
Prerequisite: Certificate IV in Community Services (or equivalent industry experience)
Core units: case management, community services context and practice, client advocacy, work within a legal and ethical framework, trauma-informed practice
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include disability support, youth work, family and domestic violence response)
Mandatory work placement: approximately 240 hours, arranged/negotiated by South Metropolitan TAFE, documented via vocational placement logbook
Compliance requirements: Working With Children Check and National Police Clearance required before placement; students must be 18+

name: Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
description:
This diploma only opens up once a student already holds the Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care. It's a deliberate two-stage pathway rather than a standalone entry qualification, which means every student arrives with at least some paid or supervised experience already in a childcare setting. The diploma itself runs across two stages, each carrying 360 hours of mandatory work placement, for a combined 720 hours of supervised field experience across the qualification, a substantial practical component relative to the classroom time.

South Metro TAFE structures the course to work around people already employed in the sector: full-time study runs at roughly two days a week (or one evening at the Rockingham campus for students working in a regulated childcare service), and those students can count their paid work hours toward the placement requirement rather than needing to find separate unpaid placement time on top of a job.

Graduates typically move into lead educator or room leader roles in long day care, and the diploma is also the recognised qualification level for meeting the "diploma-qualified educator" ratio requirements under the National Quality Framework, which is what makes it valuable to centres beyond just the individual's own skill development.
curriculum:
Prerequisite: Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care (CHC30121 or equivalent)
Stage 1: children's health, safety and wellbeing, curriculum planning for early learning, working with families and communities, 360 hours supervised work placement
Stage 2: leadership and program development, inclusive practice for children with additional needs, legal and ethical frameworks in ECEC, further 360 hours supervised work placement
Total placement: 720 hours across the diploma (working students may count paid hours in a regulated service)
Study load: approximately 2 days per week full-time (or evening delivery at Rockingham for employed students)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required

name: Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering
Diploma of Engineering - Technical
description:
This diploma (MEM50222) sits in the engineering trades pathway rather than the professional engineering pathway: it's the technical-officer-level qualification that follows on from trade or apprenticeship training, not a route toward becoming a registered engineer, which is an important distinction for students weighing this against a university engineering degree. Full-time study runs at roughly three to four days a week.

South Metro TAFE also runs this as a traineeship option, meaning eligible students can be employed under a formal training contract with an engineering or manufacturing employer and earn a wage while working through the qualification. That's a genuinely different funding and career model from full-time classroom study, and one that suits people already in the trades workforce wanting to move up without stopping work entirely.

The qualification targets specific technical roles rather than a generic "engineering" outcome: the college names CAD operator, hydraulic fitter, mechanical technician and robotics technician as typical destinations, which gives a fairly concrete sense of the mechanical/automation trades employers actually hire this diploma's graduates into.
curriculum:
Core units: engineering drawing and CAD interpretation, materials science for engineering trades, mechanical systems and components, quality and testing procedures, workplace health and safety in engineering environments
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include hydraulics and pneumatics, robotics and automation systems, CNC machining)
Delivery: full-time equivalent to 3-4 days per week; also available as a traineeship for students employed under a training contract
Typical outcomes: CAD operator, hydraulic fitter, mechanical technician, robotics technician
Pathway: foundation for further study toward Advanced Diploma of Engineering (Mechanical/Electrical)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent with Mathematics

name: Diploma of Environmental Monitoring and Technology
Diploma of Hospitality Management
description:
This diploma requires 28 units of competency (13 core plus 15 electives chosen in consultation with industry), and its most distinctive feature is where the practical training actually happens: South Metro TAFE runs students through the Bentley Pines Restaurant and Bar, a real, publicly dining venue on campus where students take on management responsibilities and serve actual paying customers rather than simulated ones. That's a genuinely different practical experience from hospitality courses that rely purely on mock service exercises.

There's no external work placement requirement, which is a little unusual for a hospitality qualification: the college's position is that the Bentley Pines operation already delivers the equivalent supervised, real-world management experience without students needing to source an outside venue and juggle two sets of rostering and assessment expectations.

Career outcomes the college points to include function manager, restaurant manager and front office manager roles, all management-track positions rather than entry-level service jobs, reflecting that this is the "management" diploma rather than the operational Certificate III/IV level that precedes it in the hospitality qualification ladder.
curriculum:
Core units (13): financial management for hospitality venues, staff rostering and workforce planning, WHS management in hospitality, quality customer service, licensing and compliance for hospitality operations
Elective units (15, industry-consulted): food and beverage service management, event and function coordination, revenue and yield management, front office operations
Practical component: face-to-face management practice in the Bentley Pines Restaurant and Bar (on-campus, open to the public)
No external work placement requirement
Total: 28 units of competency; typical outcomes include function manager, restaurant manager, front office manager

name: Diploma of Information Technology (Advanced Networking)
description:
This diploma assumes students already have hands-on networking competence before day one: the college is explicit that applicants should already be comfortable deploying and configuring virtual machines, subnetting, and configuring switches and routers, and points people without that background toward the Certificate IV in IT (Networking) first. That's a more practical entry bar than a generic "must have completed Year 12" requirement, and it keeps the diploma cohort at a more consistent skill level than open-entry courses often achieve.

Every SM TAFE diploma-level IT unit set folds in cyber security awareness, client management and professional ethics regardless of specialisation, so networking students aren't learning switch configuration in isolation from the security and client-facing skills that actual network administrator jobs require day to day.

The course is squarely vocational rather than theoretical. The training is built around current industry equipment and standards rather than networking theory divorced from what employers are actually running, which suits students aiming directly at network administrator, IT support or junior systems engineer roles rather than further academic study.
curriculum:
Prerequisite skills (or Certificate IV in IT - Networking): VM deployment and configuration, subnetting, switch and router configuration
Core units: advanced network design and implementation, network security and threat management, server administration, cloud infrastructure fundamentals
Cross-diploma units (all SM TAFE IT diplomas): cyber security awareness, working in teams, client management skills, ethics and privacy in IT
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry, aligned to current networking equipment and standards
No formal industry placement; hands-on lab-based assessment using current networking hardware

name: Diploma of Nursing
description:
This is the qualification that produces Enrolled Nurses in Western Australia: a genuinely different clinical scope from the Registered Nurse pathway that runs through university, and South Metro TAFE builds the course around human biology, medical terminology, pharmacology and person-centred care rather than the broader theory base of a nursing degree. Placement here is not optional or arranged loosely: it's mandatory for completion, and the college organises it directly rather than leaving students to find their own healthcare facility.

The placement conditions are worth being upfront about because they surprise some students: shifts run across the full week including public holidays, in week-long blocks, and can be rostered morning, afternoon or night, a genuine simulation of shift-work nursing rather than a business-hours internship. Facilities used for placement can be up to a 45-minute drive from campus, and transport and parking costs during placement are the student's own responsibility, which matters for people budgeting around a full-time study load.

Every student is issued a clinical placement handbook to document progress and works under the direct supervision of a nominated registered nurse throughout, a structured, closely supervised model reflecting how much is genuinely at stake in nursing placements compared with most other vocational diplomas.
curriculum:
Core units: human biosciences for nursing, medication administration and pharmacology, person-centred nursing care, mental health nursing, chronic and complex care, professional and legal requirements for enrolled nurses
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (may include palliative care, perioperative nursing, or maternal and child health)
Mandatory clinical placement: arranged directly by South Metropolitan TAFE, week-long shift blocks including weekends/public holidays and morning/afternoon/night shifts, supervised by a registered nurse, documented via clinical placement handbook
Compliance and logistics: placement facilities may be up to 45 minutes from campus; transport/parking costs are the student's responsibility
On completion: eligible for registration as an Enrolled Nurse with AHPRA
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, National Police Check and Working with Children Check required

name: Diploma of Photography and Digital Imaging
Diploma of Screen and Media
description:
This diploma runs with named specialisation streams rather than a single generalist screen production pathway. Options at South Metro TAFE have included animation, gaming, visual effects and immersive media production on one hand, and specialist make-up services for film, television and live theatre events on the other, which is a wider spread than most screen diplomas offer under one course code. Students effectively pick a lane early rather than sampling broadly across all of screen and media production.

Full-time study runs at roughly three days a week of scheduled attendance, but the college is explicit that students should expect an additional 25% of self-directed work on top of that: portfolio pieces, render time for animation and VFX work, or practice sessions for make-up students, none of which fits neatly into scheduled class hours the way theory-based subjects do.

The training environment is built around industry-standard software and equipment rather than education-only tools, which matters in a field where employers screening entry-level hires often look directly at a demo reel or portfolio rather than a transcript. The diploma's value is largely in what students can show, not just what units they completed.
curriculum:
Core units: screen and media industry practice, pre-production and concept development, digital production techniques, project management for screen and media
Specialisation stream (varies by intake): Animation, Gaming and Visual Effects — 3D modelling, animation principles, compositing and visual effects, game asset development
OR Specialist Make-Up Services — character and creature make-up, prosthetics, make-up for film/TV and live theatre production
Capstone: portfolio or showreel project demonstrating specialisation competencies
Study load: approximately 3 days/week scheduled attendance plus an additional 25% self-directed work (portfolio development, render/practice time)
